title: Measurement induced faster symmetry restoration in quantum trajectories
summary: Symmetries play a central role in quantum systems by protecting robust physical features, enabling noise resilient subspaces. Here, the authors propose an efficient mechanism for restoring global (1) symmetry in initially symmetry-broken states through continuous measurements of global and local observables. Here, the restoration time scale depends sensitively on the structure of the initial state. The authors also demonstrate the restoration of (2) symmetry through continuous measurements. These findings establish continuous measurement as a versatile tool for dynamically restoring symmetries.

title: Hole occupation number dependence of the $g$-tensor anisotropy and spin-orbit effects in planar silicon hole quantum dots
summary: Silicon hole dots can host dense arrays of spin qubits and provide rapid electric control via the strong spin-orbit interaction. The impact on hole-spin properties due to changes in the electrical environment, such as hole dot number, is not well understood. This study utilizes spin leakage current to probe the spin-orbit and -tensor orientation in a silicon double dot when the dot hole number is varied. The spin-orbit coupling orientation was found to be in-plane (ϕ=2.5°), and changes in hole dot occupancy had little to no effect on the spin-orbit and -tensor properties, promoting silicon hole spins as robust qubit candidates.

title: Magnetic anisotropy, first-order metamagnetic transitions, and weak antilocalization in the candidate topological semimetal ${\mathrm{Tb}}_{2}{\mathrm{Zn}}_{17}$
summary: Tb Zn crystallizes in the rhombohedral Th Zn -type structure (space group ), a structure type known to accommodate atomic disorder. Here, the authors highlight the role of disorder-induced scattering in magnetotransport measurements, which exhibit signatures of weak antilocalization. This compound shows multiple first-order field-induced metamagnetic transitions, strong magnetic anisotropy, crystal electric field effects, and possible spin canting within its antiferromagnetic state. First-principles calculations predict multiple electron and hole Fermi pockets, along with mirror-symmetry-protected nodal rings, suggesting Tb Zn as a promising rare-earth-based magnetic topological semimetal.

title: Fermi-surface-driven linear magnetoresistance in the kagome magnet ${\mathrm{TbMn}}_{6}{\mathrm{Sn}}_{6}$
summary: Here, the authors identify a Fermi surface driven mechanism for positive linear magnetoresistance in the kagome ferrimagnet TbMn Sn . Measurements on multiple nanoflake devices reveal pronounced linear magnetoresistance, with substantial device-to-device variations in both its slope and the quadratic-to-linear crossover field. Combining magnetotransport experiments with first-principles-based semiclassical calculations, the authors demonstrate how the relaxation time and small shifts in chemical potential govern these variations. These findings provide insight into the microscopic origin of linear magnetoresistance and, in particular, its emergence at relatively low crossover fields.
